analysis.summary: The PR contains high-severity bugs related to missing mandatory query parameters in frontend-to-BFF calls and inconsistent API response mapping in the Garage BFF, which will lead to runtime failures and empty data displays.

bugs.title: Mandatory 'preview' parameter missing in frontend fetch utilities
bugs.description: In several frontend utility files (fetch-app-model, fetch-garage, fetch-change-garage), the 'preview' variable is destructured but subsequently omitted from the URLSearchParams object. Because the BFF Zod schemas require 'preview' as a non-optional parameter, all requests to these endpoints will fail with a 400 Bad Request error.
bugs.risk: This is a critical failure that prevents the Feature App from loading its configuration or fetching any garage data, effectively breaking the entire feature.

bugs.title: Inconsistent response mapping in GET Garage BFF
bugs.description: The response mapping for 'get-garage' was updated to look for 'entries' directly under 'response-data', removing the '.output' property. However, the 'delete-garage' handler in the same PR still relies on 'response-data.output'. This inconsistency suggests the mapping in 'get-garage' is incorrect for the shared API structure.
bugs.risk: If the underlying AWS API maintains the '.output' wrapper (as suggested by the delete-garage code), the 'productsInGarage' variable will resolve to an empty array, causing the garage to appear empty to users even when items exist.

notBugs.topic: Switch from Mulesoft to AWS API
notBugs.reason: The change from 'endpoints.mulesoft' to 'apiEndpoint' and the associated header changes are part of a deliberate infra migration from Mulesoft to an internal AWS integration layer.
The migration from aws-simple to SST (Serverless Stack) for deployment and secret management is an architectural choice and consistent across the changed files.
Wrapping the app in GarageModelProvider and introducing a Context is a standard React pattern to avoid prop drilling and is implemented correctly.
